cleanIntro: Henry's H004 book, which covers the Golden Boy and Golden Boy Silver. Mechanically it is the same tube-fed 1/4-cock .22 as the H001, with one instruction that is unique to this model and easy to get backwards: the decorative receiver and butt plate must be wiped DRY, never oiled.

steps.title: Hammer to the Safety position, inner magazine tube withdrawn
steps.action: Put the hammer in the Safety position, then point the muzzle up or somewhere safe and draw the inner magazine tube fully out. Tip the rifle down and let the rounds run out into a container. Keep hold of the knob as the tube frees — it is under spring pressure and will leave the tube smartly if you let go.
steps.quote: To unload the magazine the hammer should be resting in the Safety position. With the rifle pointing upward or in a safe direction, completely withdraw the inner magazine tube from the gun. Tip the rifle downward, allowing the cartridges to slide out into a suitable container.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY GOLDEN BOY RIFLE, p.10

steps.title: Lever cycled repeatedly, chamber looked at
steps.action: Cycle the lever several times rather than once. Draining the magazine tube says nothing about the chamber or about a round already lifted onto the carrier. Then look at the chamber directly through the side ejection port and confirm it is empty metal before you go any further.
steps.quote: Cycle the action multiple times to be positive that no live rounds remain in the rifle. Visually inspect the chamber to ensure the rifle is unloaded.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY GOLDEN BOY RIFLE, p.10

steps.title: Action open, ammunition out of the cleaning area
steps.action: Open the action and satisfy yourself the rifle is completely empty, and keep the muzzle in a safe direction throughout. Move the ammunition out of the area before the solvent comes out — .22 rounds are small enough to get lost among cleaning kit and turn up later in the wrong place.
steps.quote: OPEN THE ACTION AND MAKE CERTAIN YOUR FIREARM IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED. KEEP THE MUZZLE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.11
steps.warn: NEVER TEST THE MECHANICAL FUNCTION OF YOUR RIFLE WITH LIVE AMMUNITION.

steps.title: Rimfire: do not dry fire it
steps.action: Do not drop the hammer on an empty chamber as a habit. The firing pin on a rimfire lands on the chamber mouth when there is no case there, and Henry warns that repeating it peens that edge until cartridges become hard to chamber and hard to extract. It is cumulative damage, so there is no single dry fire that announces itself.
steps.quote: It is suggested that you do NOT dry fire this rifle. Repeated dry firing of a rimfire can eventually peen the edge of the chamber, making it difficult to load and extract cartridges.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO LOAD YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Lever cycled forward to open the action, bore and chamber inspected
steps.action: Swing the lever forward and leave the action open — that is the working position for cleaning this rifle and no disassembly is required to reach the bore. Look into the chamber and bore and read what is there before you decide how hard to work: brass, copper and powder fouling are different problems, and ordinary powder residue is not a fault.
steps.quote: For cleaning, we suggest that you first open the action by cycling the lever forward. Inspect the chamber and bore for brass, copper and powder fouling.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Brass or nickel receiver and butt plate wiped DRY — no solvent, no oil, no wax
steps.action: This is the Golden Boy instruction that catches people. The Brasslite or nickel receiver and butt plate get a clean, soft, dust-free cloth and nothing else — no solvent, no oil, no wax. It contradicts the 'film of oil on all exposed metal' rule printed on the same page, and deliberately so: those are finished decorative surfaces, and solvent or polish will mark them permanently. Wipe them before you have solvent on your hands.
steps.quote: Important: The Golden Boy's Brasslite or Nickel receiver and butt plate should be maintained only by gently wiping with a clean, soft, dust-free cloth. Do not apply solvents, oil or wax to these surfaces.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12
steps.warn: The film-of-oil rule below applies to the barrel and the other exposed steel — NOT to the brass or nickel receiver and butt plate.

steps.title: Bore cleaned breech to muzzle, the way the bullet went
steps.action: Run the patch from the breech end out toward the muzzle, following the bullet. Cleaning the other way carries the fouling backwards out of the barrel and dumps it into the chamber and the action. A pull-through cord is the natural tool here because the Golden Boy ejects at the side and there is no straight path in from the rear.
steps.prose: To properly clean from breech to muzzle, use a pull-though cleaning kit, such as those available on www.henrypride.com.
steps.quote: WHENEVER POSSIBLE, CLEAN THE BORE IN THE DIRECTION OF BULLET TRAVEL.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Fresh patch every pass, brush never reversed in the bore
steps.action: Present a clean face of patch on every trip through the barrel; a loaded patch just redistributes grit. If you run a brush, push it right out of the muzzle before drawing it back — turning a brush around inside the bore bends the bristles the wrong way and finishes the brush.
steps.quote: NOTE: USE A CLEAN PATCH EACH TIME YOU GO DOWN THE BARREL. NEVER GO BACK AND FORTH REVERSING THE BRUSH.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

steps.title: Bolt wiped and lightly oiled
steps.action: Wipe the bolt down with solvent on a patch or rag until the carbon around the firing-pin hole lifts, then oil it lightly. Keep it light: a wet bolt in a .22 picks up unburnt powder and the mixture behaves like grinding paste in the action.
steps.quote: Wipe the bolt clean of any debris with solvent and a patch or small rag. Lightly oil bolt.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is the routine Henry publishes for the Golden Boy, and the book says plainly the rifle need not come apart to stay clean. The Deep Clean branch follows Henry's own receiver-cover procedure if you want inside — buttstock first, then the four cover screws. Past that point the book sends you to a gunsmith.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT - PLEASE NOTE THAT IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO TAKE YOUR HENRY LEVER ACTION APART TO KEEP IT CLEAN.
steps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

deepSteps.title: Tang screw and buttstock off, then the four receiver cover screws
deepSteps.action: Henry gives the order in one sentence and it matters: tang screw out and buttstock off FIRST, then the four receiver cover screws, then lift the cover. The tang screw runs through the rear of the cover, so the cover is locked down until the stock is off. Lift the cover straight up over a tray — the parts underneath are not captive.
deepSteps.aside: PLEASE SEE THE ILLUSTRATION OF PARTS ON P. 24-25
deepSteps.quote: SHOULD YOU WISH TO TAKE IT APART, UNSCREW THE RECEIVER COVER TANG SCREW AND REMOVE THE BUTTSTOCK FIRST. THEN UNSCREW THE FOUR RECEIVER COVER SCREWS AND LIFT OFF THE RECEIVER COVER WHICH WILL EXPOSE THE INTERNAL PARTS.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

deepSteps.title: Exposed internals wiped, nothing further dismantled
deepSteps.action: Clean the fouling out of the opened receiver and off the parts now in reach, then re-oil lightly and put the cover back. Do not start driving pins or lifting the fire-control parts out — Henry stops the owner-level procedure at the cover, and the fitted inner mechanism is what gives a Henry its action feel.
deepSteps.quote: NOTICE! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.12

deepSteps.title: Long storage: oil the steel, leave the brass dry
deepSteps.action: For extended storage oil the bore, chamber and internal surfaces with a firearm preservative and put anti-rust oil on the exposed steel — but the brass or nickel receiver and butt plate still get a dry cloth only. Do not seal the rifle in anything airtight and do not plug the barrel; both hold moisture against the metal.
deepSteps.caution: The no-solvent, no-oil, no-wax rule for the Brasslite or nickel receiver and butt plate still applies in storage.
deepSteps.quote: If your firearm is to be stored for an extended period, the bore, chamber and internal surfaces should be oiled with a high-quality lubricating oil or preservative intended for firearms.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H004 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — MAINTENANCE BEFORE STORAGE, p.13

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Pull a solvent-damp patch breech to muzzle, following bullet travel
Fresh patch face each pass until it comes out clean
Dry the bore and leave a light film of oil

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe carbon off the bolt face and body, then oil lightly
Wipe the carrier and the reachable receiver interior with the lever open
Keep solvent away from the trigger mechanism

cleaning.name: BRASS / NICKEL SURFACES — DRY ONLY
tasks: Wipe the Brasslite or nickel receiver with a clean, soft, dust-free cloth
Wipe the butt plate the same way
Apply no solvent, no oil and no wax to either

reassembly: Set the receiver cover on and start all four cover screws before tightening any.
Refit the buttstock and tighten the tang screw last so the cover pulls square as it seats.
Reinstall the inner magazine tube until fully seated and twist to lock; it is under spring tension.
Wipe any handling marks off the brass or nickel with a dry cloth once your hands are clean of oil.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, cycle the lever through its full travel several times and confirm it runs smoothly, check the inner magazine tube is seated and locked, and confirm the hammer sets into the Safety position and will not fall from it when the trigger is pulled.
